# Welcome

This is the companion tutorial for:

Gehling GM, Heinsberg LW. *Partnering with Generative Artificial Intelligence for Quantitative Data Analysis in Nursing Research: A Practical Workflow for Ethical Collaboration.* Biological Research for Nursing. Submitted 2026.

This guide was adapted from a presentation delivered at the International Society of Nurses in Genetics (ISONG) Annual Meeting. Originally presented as: 
Heinsberg LW. *Partnering with AI for Genomic Informatics: Practical Workflows for Data Analysis and Interpretation.* Expert Lecture; International Society of Nurses in Genetics; November 2025; Montreal, Canada.

## How to Use This Tutorial

Use the table of contents in the upper left corner to jump to any section (e.g., Overview, Code of Conduct, Application, Generative AI Disclosure), or click the arrow in the bottom right corner to move through the tutorial sequentially.

This tutorial walks through a two-phase workflow for responsible human-GenAI collaboration in quantitative data analysis, illustrated through a nursing-focused genomic research example. The code runs end-to-end, with example prompts, illustrative AI responses, and key takeaways shown in colored callout boxes throughout. Here's what to expect:

::: {.callout-note title="Our Prompt"}
This is an example of how a human prompt will appear.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="AI Response"}
This is an example of how an AI-generated illustrative response will appear.
:::

::: {.callout-important title="Important"}
This is an example of how important information, such as core principles in action, will appear throughout the tutorial.
:::

Every value generated and analyzed in this tutorial is randomly simulated and does **not** represent any real research participant. This document exists solely to demonstrate the *structure of the data* and the *analytical code* used in the workflow, so that the workflow is transparent and reproducible.

## Source Code

This tutorial's source code is maintained separately from this site and is publicly available on GitHub at [https://github.com/gmgehling/ai-genomics-workflow-tutorial](https://github.com/gmgehling/ai-genomics-workflow-tutorial).
